name: Pan-Celticism
summary: Pan-Celticism promotes solidarity and cooperation among the Celtic nations (Irish, Scots, Welsh, Bretons, Cornish and Manx), grounded in shared Celtic languages and heritage and in resistance to Anglicisation and Gallicisation. It ranges from cultural exchange to demands for self-government, independence and an eventual confederation of Celtic states. Language revival is its central practical concern, and its modern political form works by peaceful, non-sectarian means. It has no programme on economics or social morality.
scope: The mainstream of the movement as shown by the Celtic League (founded 1961, the main political body), the cultural Celtic Congress (from 1900/1917) and the nineteenth-century language-nationalism associated with Thomas Davis; the early Celtic Association and its founders. Excludes the Celtic race theories of the early twentieth century and the Celtic-reconstructionist religious revival. Most statements fall outside the movement's concerns, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Pan-Celtic bodies have no health policy; the League's call to use national resources for all a country's people and the social-democratic leanings of Celtic-nation nationalist parties suggest mild support.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No stated wage policy; inferred from the League's aim of national resources benefiting all people and from left-of-centre Celtic nationalist politics.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Never addressed; the stress on resources serving each people rather than outside interests suggests mild scepticism of unregulated markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Not addressed directly; the aim of using each country's resources for the benefit of all its people is inferred to lean toward public stewardship.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No tax programme exists; inferred from the movement's communal, peripheral and mildly egalitarian outlook.

unions-good.rationale: Pan-Celtic sources say nothing on unions; Celtic nationalists have often allied with labour movements, so mild agreement is inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Neither the cultural congresses nor the League address property rights, and adherents span the political spectrum.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Unaddressed; inferred from the aim of national resources serving local peoples rather than outside owners.

cut-welfare.rationale: No welfare position stated; adherents mainly sit in social-democratic nationalist traditions, so cuts are inferred to be disfavoured.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ruaraidh Erskine floated a Celtic socialism but this is not a mainstream pan-Celtic demand, so adherents are split or indifferent.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the League's non-violent civil-liberties stance on national freedom suggests mild distrust of state surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Entirely outside the movement's concerns, with no basis for a direction.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by pan-Celtic sources and adherents hold varied views.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement is a federative, cooperative and diversity-respecting project, so a strong leader bypassing gridlock fits poorly.

state-harmful.rationale: Pan-Celtic aims are about winning states or self-government for Celtic nations, so adherents do not regard the state as unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed and varies between Celtic nations.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; the League's peaceful-means framing and campaigning against militarisation of Celtic lands suggests mild disagreement.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Outside the scope of the movement.

decide-locally.rationale: The League seeks self-governance for each Celtic nation, and its view that it is secondary to national organisations stresses subsidiarity.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by any pan-Celtic source.

traditional-family.rationale: Movement is cultural and national; adherents range from Catholic traditionalists to secular progressives.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is religiously mixed and its modern organisations are not defined by social-moral positions.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed and Celtic nations differ, with Catholic and Protestant strands among adherents.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement was explicitly interdenominational with sectarian differences a known obstacle, so a larger public religious role is mildly disfavoured.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's own concern is historic cultural and linguistic injustice, not racial.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Preserving each Celtic nation's culture, music and languages is the movement's central purpose, as in the Celtic Congress's object to perpetuate Celtic culture and ideals.

gradual-change.rationale: The League seeks self-governance by peaceful stages but also independence, so adherents split between gradualism and radical change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The League defines Celtic nations by language and culture rather than by blood, and nothing suggests restriction; mild disagreement is inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The League holds UN consultative status and seeks UN-world recognition for small nations, but also demands sovereignty, so adherents are split.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is not addressed; adherents range widely.

nation-first.rationale: Self-government for Celtic nations suggests putting national interests first, but pan-Celtic solidarity is internationalist, so it is split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The League's peaceful-means stance and small-nation outlook suggest scepticism of armed intervention.

open-borders.rationale: National self-government for distinct peoples implies borders matter, though the movement is not hostile to migration.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a pan-Celtic topic; no documented position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Neither the Celtic League nor the Congress takes a view on technological progress, so adherents are split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from the League's long record of campaigning on environmental and nuclear issues in Celtic lands, which was not confirmed in the pages read.

revolution-justified.rationale: Adherents ranged from cultural revivalists to militants after the 1916 Rising, while the League is peaceful, so it is split.

experts-over-public.rationale: The movement is a popular cultural nationalism, so rule by experts over the public is disfavoured.

central-planning.rationale: No economic system is advocated beyond Erskine's occasional Celtic socialism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Pan-Celtic sources never discuss how businesses should be owned, so there is no basis for a direction.

land-value-tax.rationale: Fiscal design is outside the cultural and constitutional concerns of the movement.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No pan-Celtic source mentions inheritance or estate taxation.

basic-income.rationale: Income-support schemes are not part of any pan-Celtic programme; adherents hold varied views.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is not addressed; protecting small national economies could appeal but no source says so.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Only the aim of using national resources for all the people is stated, which does not decide the question.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed in any pan-Celtic source.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A cultural-national movement with no anti-money agenda; Erskine's Celtic socialism was never a mainstream demand.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; the movement has no monetary radicalism and its Celtic state proposals include a joint development bank.

one-party-rule.rationale: The League is explicitly non-sectarian and committed to peaceful, plural self-government, and the movement has no single-party model.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The article notes no pan-Celtic monarchy position; Tudor and Stewart Celtic claims accompanied Anglicisation, and independence movements here are mostly republican or ambivalent.

democracy-best.rationale: The League seeks freedom through peaceful, political means and self-government, which implies democratic rule.

direct-votes.rationale: The League backs independence referendums but has no general stance on direct legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: No council-communist strand exists in pan-Celticism.

right-to-secede.rationale: The League advocates ultimately an independent state for each Celtic nation, which means secession from the UK and France, and it backs referendums.

natural-rulers.rationale: The movement is popular and national, not elitist, though early leaders were gentry and scholars.

political-violence-never.rationale: The League works by peaceful means, but the wider movement included militants and the pages read do not state an absolute rule.

war-builds-character.rationale: The League stresses peaceful means and the cultural movement has no cult of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Sectarian division between Protestant and Catholic Celts hampered the movement, so a non-sectarian civic order is favoured.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: No pan-Celtic claim for scriptural law; the movement is non-sectarian across Catholic and Protestant lines.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Self-government by Celtic states is the aim, so state courts and defence are assumed.

military-superiority.rationale: Small nations seeking independence by peaceful means do not aim at superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The League defines a Celtic nation by a living Celtic language rather than descent, and the article notes the racial claims of earlier rhetoric did not hold up.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement sees nations, language and culture as the key units, not class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The movement seeks equality between peoples and languages, not a position on individual outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Self-government for peoples over their national territories is the core aim, which is close to this idea.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Celtic nationalists describe Anglicisation as conquest but no reparations demand is documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement unites the Celtic nations on shared ancestry, language family and heritage, with a proposed confederation, though not by religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement is communal and solidaristic, with the League stressing special relationship and solidarity between peoples.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Romantic revival tied people to land and landscape, but no clear position on nature's intrinsic value exists.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy has never been a pan-Celtic concern, though depopulation of Gaelic heartlands worries some.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The revival romanticised tradition but no pan-Celtic source condemns industrial civilization.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The revival looks to heritage and language, with no stated stance on speeding technological change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics lies entirely outside the movement's aims.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; a community-based cultural movement would be unlikely to favour it.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is not addressed in any pan-Celtic source.

restore-past-order.rationale: The revival drew on a romantic past, but aims are modern self-government and language revival, not restoration of a social order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement is itself identity-driven, but it has no stated view on pragmatism versus ideology.

direct-action.rationale: Mixed: the League works by peaceful campaigning and referendums, while other adherents used protest and activism.

means-match-ends.rationale: The League's commitment to peaceful means for freedom implies methods consistent with the free society sought.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A modern cultural-political movement that has no primitivist element. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: No such radical economic aim exists in the movement.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution rules are not discussed; the League says only that national resources should benefit all the people.

production-for-use.rationale: The League's aim of resources benefiting all the people gives no verdict on profit versus use in production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not addressed beyond occasional Celtic-socialist thinking.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contradicts the League's peaceful, non-sectarian approach and the movement's national rather than class orientation.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; inferred disfavour as the movement idealised rural communities of small owners.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Pan-Celtic literature blames conquest and centralising states for suppression, not capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement aims to build self-governing states, which tax, and has no libertarian strand.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal-philosophical limits on state power are not discussed in pan-Celtic sources.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement claims collective rights of nations and language communities to survive, which conflicts with rights belonging only to individuals.

conscription.rationale: Peaceful-means stance and small-nation outlook suggest disfavour, though not documented.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement pursues political voice and self-government rather than exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; a communal movement would reject citizens-as-customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The League speaks of political, cultural, social and economic freedom, but no philosophical claim is stated.

media-academia-power.rationale: Pan-Celtic sources contain no claim about universities or media dominating politics.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The article describes the 1930s Celtic race research as vague and unsupported, and modern Celtic organisations define identity by language, not heredity.

organic-representation.rationale: Not a pan-Celtic position; the movement works through parliamentary self-government.

total-state.rationale: Incompatible with the League's non-sectarian, peaceful and diversity-respecting self-government. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

national-rebirth.rationale: The revival and resurgence of Celtic languages and cultures after Anglicisation is its central theme, though not a doctrine of decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Celtic nations are small and seek only self-government within their own territories.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: No feudal element exists in the modern movement. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

bound-labor.rationale: No pan-Celtic source supports serfdom. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is not part of the movement; Celtoscepticism debates about the Celts concern archaeology, not this thesis.

universal-morality.rationale: Pan-Celtic sources are silent on moral universalism, and adherents are religiously mixed.

single-common-good.rationale: The League explicitly allows diversity to express itself, but beyond that there is no doctrine on a single common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The movement does not address this and adherents vary.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The League has diaspora branches but no stated return-right policy.

revive-national-language.rationale: Reinstating the Celtic languages is the League's stated emphasis, and Davis held that a people without its language is only half a nation.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Industrial governance is not a pan-Celtic topic.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; language-medium schooling is wanted but not through vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic policy is not addressed by the cultural or political pan-Celtic bodies.

economic-freedom.rationale: The League asks for economic freedom for the Celtic nations as nations, but says nothing on the link between economic and political liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Davis relied on elite example for language revival, but this is not a general theory of rule.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination for each Celtic people is a core theme, and the League advocates an independent state in its own right for each nation.

force-without-un.rationale: The League's peaceful stance and UN consultative status suggest respect for UN authority over unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; Romantic movement valued tradition and feeling alongside scholarship.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility has no pan-Celtic position; the League defines nations by language, not citizenship status.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not addressed by any pan-Celtic source.

class-collaboration.rationale: Not addressed; the movement united classes behind a national cause.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Celtic Congress exists to perpetuate Celtic culture, so sacrificing cultural institutions is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Celtic nations see themselves as dominated within the UK and France and seek solidarity among peoples, though not a front of countries against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Pan-Celticism is national but cross-border by design; it does not discuss how workers should organise.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: No such claim in the movement and modern organisations are secular-liberal in tone.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; no pan-Celtic source supports banning interest and Celtic development-bank ideas assume lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The League is non-sectarian and defines nations by language; there is no segregationist element.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Pan-Celtic accounts treat the state as a conqueror of peoples rather than as a class tool, and do not take a class-analytic view.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not addressed in the sources read, and branches differ by country.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: A movement defending minority cultures against assimilation is unlikely to demand assimilation of others, though it expects respect for local languages.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of this kind has no place in pan-Celtic sources. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

proportional-representation.rationale: Voting systems are not discussed in pan-Celtic sources, though Celtic-nation parties often favour PR in practice.

national-mission.rationale: Small nations seeking freedom have no mission of exporting their system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender analysis is outside the movement's published aims.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Early nationalists were hostile to ruling centres but no general position exists.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No eugenics element in the League's stated aims, and 1930s race research is judged unsupported. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for state killings is not a pan-Celtic doctrine, though it arises in Irish and Breton contexts.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The League wants states that use national resources for all the people, which goes beyond minimal government.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts the League's non-sectarian language-based definition of nationhood.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Non-sectarian principle and the aim of freedom for all Celtic peoples imply equal standing, though the matter is rarely stated.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist strategy debates have no place in pan-Celtic sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is not an issue for the movement, which is non-sectarian.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The movement was interdenominational and no source supports restriction.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed and religion divided Celtic countries.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine unrelated to pan-Celtic thought.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Self-determination and peaceful campaigning for self-government rest on consent, as in the League's backing of referendums.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance is not a pan-Celtic concern.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to the League's non-sectarian peaceful principles.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The League is peaceful but the wider movement is not libertarian and this absolutist formulation is not claimed.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement stresses solidarity and cooperation among peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party-ban questions are not discussed in pan-Celtic sources.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Celtic nationalists describe Anglicisation as domination by larger neighbours, which fits this notion of freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design beyond self-government is not discussed in the sources read.

vanguard-party.rationale: No vanguard concept in the movement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The League's aim of benefiting all the people does not prioritise the poor specifically.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are a UK domestic issue with no pan-Celtic position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Industrial relations law lies outside the movement's scope.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Pan-Celtic sources attribute hardship to conquest and centralisation, with no population thesis stated.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The League states it allows diversity to express itself within it, and it champions linguistic diversity, though not specifically ethnic.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in pan-Celtic sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the League's peaceful, freedom-oriented aims.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price regulation is not part of any pan-Celtic programme.

party-controls-media.rationale: Contradicts the free, plural movement; the League promotes publications in all Celtic languages by voluntary means.

party-commands-army.rationale: No party-army doctrine exists, and the League is peaceful. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not addressed; the League defines nations by language and culture.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Politicians' pay is not a pan-Celtic topic.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party rules are not addressed; the League is a federation of branches, not a party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Post-Brexit proposals envisage a voluntary Celtic confederation and the League seeks formal association of Celtic nations, though not an EU stance.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; parliamentary self-government is assumed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed and church traditions differ among Celts.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement was interdenominational and sectarian rule would split it.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist slogan that pan-Celtic thinkers did not take up.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The movement promotes arts and music festivals and has no censorship programme.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Executive term limits are not addressed in pan-Celtic sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall mechanisms are not discussed in the sources read.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed, though small-nation neutralism has appeal in some branches.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not a pan-Celtic issue.

people-in-arms.rationale: Peaceful means and no militia tradition in the pan-Celtic programme.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Celtic revival romanticised rural, Gaelic-speaking heartlands, but no morality claim about cities is stated.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Irish reunification and cross-border unity are favoured by many adherents and Celtic League Irish members, but it is not a defined pan-Celtic plank.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was largely led by scholars and educated activists.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The movement claims equal standing for small Celtic cultures against assimilation into a dominant one, which implies cultural equality.

death-penalty.rationale: Criminal punishment is not addressed, and adherents come from countries that long since abolished it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School sex education is not addressed; adherents include Catholics and secular liberals.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The movement is scholarly in orientation and has no creationist element.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed by any pan-Celtic source.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The League defines nations by language and culture not by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: The League places particular emphasis on promoting the Celtic languages and the Congress is built around Celtic languages as minority tongues.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities are not discussed, though the movement is non-sectarian.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style individualism is not part of pan-Celtic thought.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; the movement concerns European Celtic nations, not poor-country debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The League seeks political, cultural, social and economic freedom but does not demand systemic economic transformation.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Freedom is the League's stated central aim.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Development aid is outside the movement's aims.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from peaceful stance and small-nation outlook; the pages read did not state an anti-nuclear position.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential selection is not addressed in pan-Celtic sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not a pan-Celtic issue, apart from a post-Brexit idea of a Celtic development bank.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not a pan-Celtic topic; a peaceful movement would lean to compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The League's aim of using national resources for the benefit of all the people suggests that property serves the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist debate unrelated to pan-Celticism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation doctrine is not discussed in the sources read.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliances are not addressed; the movement is peaceful and cultural.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Celtic nationalists see conquest and incorporation as unjust, but no stance on this principle is stated.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; interdenominational outlook disfavours state control of churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Head-of-state arrangements are not addressed, and Celtic nations have both monarchy and republic.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Adherents seek secession by consent and peaceful means, so force to prevent regions leaving is opposed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Self-governance within a larger union as a step toward independence is the League's advocated path, with the Celtic confederation as an option.

sacred-ruler.rationale: No pan-Celtic doctrine of sacred rulers; Tudor and Stewart monarchs claimed Celtic descent while Anglicising. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not addressed in pan-Celtic sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature versus nurture is not a pan-Celtic topic; the old racial claims were rejected by modern researchers.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Contradicts the movement's constitutional, peaceful self-government. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy has nothing to do with the movement.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed in pan-Celtic sources.

leader-cult.rationale: No leader cult in pan-Celtic organisations, which are federations of national branches. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are outside the movement's scope.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is not a pan-Celtic aim, though land questions mattered in Irish and Highland nationalism.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is about Celtic nations, not refugee conflicts.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The League defines nations by language not descent and seeks only self-government within existing nations' territories.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: No pan-Celtic source supports religious penalties, and the movement is non-sectarian.

women-must-cover.rationale: Alien to the movement. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not a stated aim; the post-Brexit confederation proposals do not specify a currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The core project is political and cultural cooperation among peoples sharing Celtic languages and ancestry, with a formal association or confederation as the goal.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Pan-Celtic thinkers insisted that each Celtic people keep its own national space and culture, though the League's aim goes further to independence.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The movement treats language, culture and identity as drivers rather than economics.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is outside the movement's concerns.

no-bailouts.rationale: Financial rescue policy is not addressed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; a minority-defending movement tends to favour limits on majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not part of any pan-Celtic programme.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement's international cooperation and proposals for a Celtic development bank do not point to autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-treaty standards are not discussed in pan-Celtic sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Maoist and Guevarist idea with no place in pan-Celtic writing.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The League seeks freedom by peaceful means.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The pan-Celtic sources record Celtic-descent claims by Tudor and Stewart monarchs but take no position on titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Pan-Celtic revival centres Celtic history and language in education against Anglocentric curricula.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Davis and the movement see rule by a more powerful neighbour as conquest that suppressed the native language, the opposite of tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Davis wanted schools to teach and extend the national language and national pride, though the topic of flags and anthems is not addressed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is not part of the movement's concerns.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed in the sources read.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Crisis theory is not part of pan-Celtic thought.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Celtic nations were subjected to empire and have no imperial legacy to cultivate.

delink-world-market.rationale: The movement is internationalist among small nations and proposes joint institutions, not delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist concept that pan-Celtic writing does not use.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The League is non-sectarian, which opposes discriminating on religious grounds.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Pan-Celtic sources do not discuss constitutional entrenchment, though language rights are a likely subject.
